$schema_note: ECS Fargate task definition for the ReciterAI taxonomy COLD-RUN (#240; `python -m pipeline_cold.run`). The cold-run is the full-corpus taxonomy rebuild — 10 sequential stages (score → assign → discover[no-op] → relabel → top_topic → count → rollup → feedback_sweep → backfill_spotlight[--publish] → publish_hierarchy, `pipeline_cold/run.py:94-185`) ending in the two prod publishes (spotlight.json → wcmc-reciterai-artifacts, hierarchy.json → wcmc-reciterai-hierarchy). It is on-demand and operator-gated (no EventBridge schedule — see infra/README.md 'Cold-run launch path'). REUSES THE SAME IMAGE as the daily-enrichment task (the repo's single Dockerfile `COPY . .` already contains pipeline_cold); this task def only OVERRIDES the default CMD to the cold-run entrypoint — no separate image build. Bedrock authenticates via the `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` bearer token (same as enrichment); the task role carries NO `bedrock:InvokeModel`. MUST run as ONE container / ONE task: the stages hand off via local files on a shared filesystem (stage `assign` writes `hierarchy_augmented_*.json`; stage `publish_hierarchy` reads them), so stages cannot be split across tasks.

placeholders.{TASK_ROLE_ARN}: arn:aws:iam::{ACCOUNT_ID}:role/reciterai-cold-task — IAM role attached to the running container; carries the policy in `cold_run_task_iam_policy.json` (DDB CRUD on `reciterai`, S3 read+write on `wcmc-reciterai-hierarchy/*` + `wcmc-reciterai-artifacts/spotlight/*`, Secrets Manager read on the DB + OpenAI secrets, CloudWatch Logs). This is a NEW role — the enrichment task role has no S3 grant and cannot be reused.
placeholders.{EXECUTION_ROLE_ARN}: arn:aws:iam::{ACCOUNT_ID}:role/ecsTaskExecutionRole — the standard ECS task execution role (reusable from the enrichment deploy). Needs ECR pull + CloudWatch Logs (AWS-managed `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy`) and an inline `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` grant on the 3 secret ARNs injected below (`reciter-analysis-db`, `openai-api-key`, `bedrock-api-key`). The execution role — not the task role — injects the `secrets[]` env vars at container start.
placeholders.{IMAGE_URI}: ECR image URI of the SAME pushed reciterai image used by the enrichment task, e.g. `{ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/reciterai-enrichment:{GIT_SHA}`. No separate build — the Dockerfile `COPY . .` already includes `pipeline_cold`; this task def overrides the default CMD. Use an image built from the commit whose `config/thresholds.json` carries the intended flag state (the flags are baked into the image — see #204 / the cold-run runbook).
placeholders.{DB_SECRET_ARN}: Full ARN of `reciterai/reciter-analysis-db` (JSON SecretString with DB_HOST/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD/DB_NAME keys). ECS pulls individual JSON keys via the trailing `:KEY::` syntax. Same secret as the enrichment task.
placeholders.{OPENAI_SECRET_ARN}: Full ARN of `reciterai/openai-api-key` (JSON SecretString with an OPENAI_API_KEY key). The Bedrock content-filter fallback (gpt-5.1). Same secret as the enrichment task.
placeholders.{BEDROCK_API_KEY_SECRET_ARN}: Full ARN of `reciterai/bedrock-api-key` (plain SecretString — a LONG-TERM Bedrock API key). boto3 auto-detects the value via `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` and uses it as the bearer token for `bedrock-runtime` calls. Same secret as the enrichment task. NOTE: this is referenced by the EXECUTION role (env injection), not the task role — the cold-run task-role policy intentionally omits it.

deploy_notes.sizing: 1 vCPU / 4 GB. The cold-run is Bedrock/IO-bound, not compute- or memory-bound: no stage loads a model or embeddings in-process (Titan embeddings are a Bedrock API call), so peak in-process memory is ~300-500 MB (`score` loads the full ~6,200-PMID corpus + author/faculty maps) and ~100-150 MB (`backfill_spotlight`). 4 GB gives headroom over that for the full-table DynamoDB scans (`top_topic`, `count`, `pool_ranker`) and the boto3/SQLAlchemy/openai dependency set under Python 3.12. 1 vCPU (vs enrichment's 0.25) is for the 15-way-concurrent Bedrock fan-out in `score`/`assign` (asyncio.Semaphore / ThreadPoolExecutor) — 0.25 vCPU would head-of-line-stall JSON parse + TLS across a multi-hour run. Valid Fargate floor for this workload is 0.5 vCPU / 2 GB; 1 vCPU / 4 GB is the comfortable choice. Default 20 GB ephemeral storage is sufficient (largest local artifact set is well under 100 MB). Wall-clock is multi-hour (~2-6h estimated; the cold-run has no measured runtime in the repo) — set any wrapping run-task monitor/timeout accordingly; do NOT block a launcher on it.

runtime_modes.dry_run_plumbing_gate: Operator `aws ecs run-task ... --overrides '{"containerOverrides":[{"name":"reciterai-cold","command":["python","-m","pipeline_cold.run","--dry-run"]}]}'`. Prints the stage plan and exits 0 without invoking any stage — proves the task def launches, the image is right, secrets land in env, the task role reaches AWS, and CloudWatch logging works. Fast and zero Bedrock cost. Use `scripts/run_cold_run.sh` with `COLD_MODE=dry-run`.
runtime_modes.full_run: Operator `aws ecs run-task ... ` with NO command override (the task def default `command` runs the full cold-run as `--initiated-by operator`). This is the real, multi-hour, publishing run. Use `scripts/run_cold_run.sh` with `COLD_MODE=run`; the script launches and returns the task ARN + monitoring commands (it does NOT block for hours).
runtime_modes.resume_from_stage: Operator `aws ecs run-task ... --overrides '{"containerOverrides":[{"name":"reciterai-cold","command":["python","-m","pipeline_cold.run","--from-stage","publish_hierarchy"]}]}'`. Resumes a cold-run that died mid-way, skipping completed stages. CAUTION: `--from-stage` relies on the local draft files from the EARLIER stages, which a NEW container does not have — only meaningful inside a re-run that re-does the draft-producing stages, or once the cold-run persists those intermediates. Treat resume as best-effort until the local-state handoff is externalized.
